annotations.text:
Snippet layer — six screens.

Reusable message text that belongs to no group, no role and no receiver. Matched to web-console's real tokens: slate-950/900/800 surfaces, cyan-400 accent, 1px white/10 borders, 8px radii, lucide icons, the same 8-swatch HEADER_COLORS used for panes and groups.

Top row is the everyday loop. Bottom row is handoff, capture and management.
The cheapest reach: a most-recently-used rail above the toolbar, opened by one control in the existing key row. No dialog, no trip to settings.
The primary home. Tap inserts at the cursor via draft.appendAtCaret — the seam voice dictation already uses. Recent / Pinned / All, and filtering matches body text, not just names.

S4, made visible. One field per distinct name, no parser and no expressions. {{cwd}} and {{session}} are filled by the console from a closed list. An unfilled name stays in the text instead of leaving a silent gap — the opposite of what renderHandoffPrompt does with an empty payload today.

The change you called out. Three sections replace `if (!groupId) return []`: the group stays the default scope, other sessions become reachable, and a new session is a target in its own right.

And the message can now come from any snippet, not only the receiving role's incoming_prompt. The role's prompt stays the default when it has one — a snippet just overrides it, exactly like the per-target edit field already does.
The affordance that makes the store fill itself. Selecting a phrase turns it into a variable, so a snippet gets its holes at the moment you already know which words change.
A tenth tab beside Templates and Handoff rules. Promote writes a governed skill in prompt-manager and then stops — one direction, no sync, snippet stays put.
